events.title: SEQUEL paper published — birth of SQL
events.summary: Chamberlin and Boyce presented SEQUEL at the 1974 ACM SIGFIDET workshop — the structured query language for IBM System R.
events.about: SQL (originally SEQUEL) is the language for reading and writing relational databases — `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `JOIN`, `GROUP BY`. Every web app, bank ledger, and analytics pipeline ultimately talks SQL or a dialect of it (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server).

narrative.whyChosen: This paper defined the declarative query language that made Codd's relational model practical on real systems.
narrative.whyImportant: SQL became the universal data-access layer — still the dominant interface to structured data fifty years later.
narrative.problemSolved: Navigational database APIs forced programmers to describe how to fetch data; SEQUEL let them describe what they wanted.

sources.title: ACM — SEQUEL: A Structured English Query Language (May 1, 1974)
